doc.text: Bottle Hydro Dates and cascade pressures

Trailer 600 (Trailer Readiness Form, 1099 Gage Gonzales, 2:59 PM) — entries #1 through #4 each read "4/25". That is a hydro date with no pressure value. Board AT# is 600, so a trailer was on location and the entries are incomplete.
Trailer 607 (Trailer Readiness Form, TYRELL SANDERS, 1:40 PM) — entries #1 through #4 each read "4500". That is a pressure with no hydro date. Board AT# is 607, so this is a valid finding.

Clean: trailer 602 (1099 Robert Henigan) "7/25 4500" on four bottles; trailer 603 (Bryan Medlin) "7/26-4500" on four; trailer 608 (1099 Bobby Galindo) "01/26 4000 psi" and "09/25 4000 psi" on four. On the H2S dailies, BOBBY FLEMING recorded "6@2200" and "4/33x6", LARRY JARAMILLO "2500" and "07/23", and JOSHUA BLASSINGAME "All 6 - 2400lb bottles full" and "4-23" — all complete.

Trailer 606 (1099 Gael Antonio Avila, 3:14 PM) — all ten entries read "425/725". The format carries both values so this is not a missing-field finding, but 425 psi against the 4000 to 4500 recorded on every other trailer today is far enough out that it is probably a typo for 4250 or 4500. Worth one question to Avila rather than a correction from here.

clean.text: NATHAN CONTRERAS filed two Trailer Inspection Forms for trailer 606 (5:27 AM Andrews shop, 7:46 PM) and two air job forms for UNIVERITY 10-3 4H and UNIVERSITY 1-32 4H, all photos on the day, complete OWL reviews, FR Yes. JORDAN LEMMONS (trailer 605), JERRY GONZALES (trailer 601) and ALEXANDER CLUBB (trailer 601) each filed a clean Trailer Inspection Form. KEELAN HAMMER closed out the EOG Jal MFA class the same day it was held. DENNIS EASLEY's Sabine Wyatt Pad field service is fully documented.

Both kinds of trailer form, and the equipment sections of the H2S daily, are photo-based. A defect visible only in a photograph would not surface in this review — I can read that an image was captured and when, but not what it shows. Fire extinguisher inspection and expiration dates, first aid kit dates and 4-gas calibration dates exist only inside images, not as text, so none of those can be checked here.

A second limitation specific to today: this review ran at 11:00 PM Central on 10/19 itself, so the usual follow-up sweep of the next morning's mail for late-arriving forms could not be run. Any 10/19 submission that lands after tonight is not in these counts, and some of the absences listed above may close by morning. One Trailer Readiness Form that arrived at 8:57 AM today carries a form date of 10/18 (trailer 603, submitted by HUMBERTO MARQUEZ-SALAZAR) — it was read, it belongs to 10/18, and it is not counted toward today's coverage.

87 of 87 submissions read. The job board was available: the 10/19/2026 ArkLaTex and Permian Basin boards from Blake Walton, received 9:59 AM Central today, were used, and 69 manned board rows were checked for coverage.
